'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[2021 Galmudug clashes]]
***The death toll from the clashes between the [[Somali Armed Forces|Somali National Army]] and [[Sufism|Sufi]] [[paramilitary]] group [[Ahlu Sunna Waljama'a]] in [[Galmudug]] increases to 120. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/somalia-death-toll-fighting-between-army-former-allied-group-rises-120-2021-10-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]], [[2019–2024 Sudanese transition to democracy|Sudanese transition to democracy]]
**[[List of heads of government of Sudan|Prime Minister]] [[Abdalla Hamdok]] and other senior members of the civilian [[Government of Sudan|government]] are detained by the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|military]] in a [[coup d'état]]. The military also seizes state television and blocks [[internet]] access. Thousands of people gather in [[Khartoum]] to protest the coup. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/25/sudan-coup-fears-amid-claims-military-have-arrested-senior-government-officials (''The Guardian'')]
**Ten civilians are killed and 140 more are injured as mass protests occur following the coup. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-59045020 (BBC News)]
**[[List of heads of state of Sudan|Chairman]] of the [[Sovereignty Council of Sudan|Sovereignty Council]] [[Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] announces a [[state of emergency]] and the dissolution of the Sovereignty Council and the government. [https://saudigazette.com.sa/article/612689/World/Al-Burhan-declares-state-of-emergency-dissolves-government (''Saudi Gazette'')]
*[[2021 Uganda bombings]]
**An explosion on a bus in [[Mpigi District]] kills one person and injures several others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/25/bus-explosion-uganda (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Expo 2020]]
**It is announced that around 1.5 million people have visited the [[Expo 2020]] event in [[Dubai]] since its opening on October 1. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/gulf/2021/10/25/Expo-2020-Dubai-records-1-5-million-visits-since-opening- (Al Arabiya)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Motor fuel|Petrol]] prices in the [[United Kingdom]] reach their highest level since April 2012, at [[Pound sterling|£]]1.4294 per litre. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-59034854 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Pacific hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Rick (2021)|Hurricane Rick]] loses strength as it moves farther inland in [[Mexico]]. The states that are most affected are [[Michoacán]] and [[Guerrero, Mexico|Guerrero]], especially the seaside city of [[Acapulco]] in Guerrero. Other states such as [[Colima]], [[Jalisco]] and [[Nayarit]] open shelters ahead of potential heavy rain. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/hurricane-rick-makes-landfall-mexicos-pacific-coast-2021-10-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Karnataka]]
*****Six districts in [[Karnataka]], [[India]] have vaccinated 90% of their population with the first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/six-districts-in-karnataka-have-jabbed-90-adults-with-first-covid-19-vaccine-dose/articleshow/87246976.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****In a near-return to normalcy, operating hours restrictions on bars and restaurants have been lifted in cities across the [[Greater Tokyo Area]] and [[Osaka]] for the first time in 11 months, also allowing these establishments to resume their [[Alcohol (drug)|alcohol]] sales at any time during their business hours as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases decreases. [https://www.asahi.com/sp/ajw/articles/14467874 (''The Asahi Shimbun'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] Health Technology Assessment Council approves the administration of a third COVID-19 vaccine as a [[booster dose]] to health workers in the fourth quarter of 2021, with other priority groups becoming eligible for a booster dose in 2022. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/philippines-eyes-covid-19-boosters-health-workers-senior-citizens-late-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reopens its primary schools after a closure of nearly five months due to the third wave of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.newsfirst.lk/2021/10/25/sri-lanka-opens-schools-for-primary-students-after-almost-five-months/ (NewsFirst)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] imposes a nationwide [[curfew]] from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. and makes [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face masks mandatory]] in all public venues in an attempt to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases. The country also begins to implement a mandatory [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic|green certificate]] for shopping malls, restaurants, public institutions and workplaces. [https://seenews.com/news/romania-tightens-covid-19-restrictions-to-tame-surge-in-covid-19-cases-758492 (See News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 37,930 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 8.279 million. [http://wam.ae/en/details/1395302984793 (Emirates News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] surpasses five million cases of COVID-19. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/health-pmn/number-of-covid-19-infections-in-spain-hits-5-million (Reuters via ''National Post'')]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[European Medicines Agency]] approves a [[booster dose]] of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for all adults over the age of 18, which can be administered at least six months after the second dose. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-business-health-public-health-coronavirus-vaccine-49990d44c40a475cd5ff056790e268fd (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] begins vaccinations for at-risk children in [[Mexico City]]. [https://www.laprensalatina.com/mexicos-vaccination-drive-for-at-risk-kids-starts-in-capital/ (La Prisna Latina)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] signs a presidential proclamation requiring international travelers to be fully vaccinated using any [[World Health Organization|WHO]]-approved COVID-19 vaccine and also allows "mix-and-match" doses. The proclamation also requires [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States|unvaccinated American]]s and immigrants to [[COVID-19 testing|test]] negative for COVID-19 one day before their departure. These rules will take effect on November 8. [https://www.ft.com/content/d0d4156d-ace9-4119-ac3e-a1e4d4bf6440 (''Financial Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea]]
***[[Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea|Prime Minister]] [[James Marape]] pleads for Papua New Guineans to get vaccinated against COVID-19 as the situation, fueled by the [[Delta variant]], worsens, with hospitals in [[Port Moresby]] and other cities operating at maximum capacity. Marape states that the death toll currently exceeds 300, but the actual total may be much higher. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/454240/png-leader-pleas-for-people-to-get-vaccinated (RNZ)]
 
'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Mali]]
**The [[government of Mali|Malian interim government]] gives the country's [[Economic Community of West African States|ECOWAS]] representative 72 hours to leave [[Mali]] over "actions incompatible with his status", though the government added that they still maintain a "willingness to work together with ECOWAS in the transition". [https://guardian.ng/news/world/mali-expels-west-african-bloc-representative/ (AFP via ''The Guardian Nigeria'')]
*International response to the [[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]], [[Sudan–United States relations]]
**Hours after the coup d'état in [[Sudan]], the [[United States Department of State]] suspends [[United States dollar|$]]700 million worth of [[United States aid to Sudan|aid to the country]] until the restoration of the civilian government. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/us-pauses-us700-million-aid-sudan-after-military-takeover-2268236 (AFP via CNA)]

'''Law and crime'''
*A court in [[Munich]], [[Germany]], [[sentence (law)|sentences]] an [[Islamic State]]-affiliated 30-year-old woman to 10 years in prison for allowing a 5-year-old [[Yazidi]] girl to die from thirst in [[Iraq]]. The woman was found guilty on multiple [[criminal charge|charges]], including some related to [[terrorism]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/german-isis-bride-sentenced-10-years-prison-yazidi-girl-slave-die-of-thirst/ (CBS News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[President of Egypt|Egyptian President]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] announces that the state of emergency, which was imposed in April 2017, will be lifted. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/25/world/middleeast/egypt-sisi-state-emergency.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[COVID-19 misinformation]]
**[[Facebook]] and [[Alphabet Inc.]], which owns [[YouTube]], announce that they have removed a video of [[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] claiming that [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s cause [[HIV/AIDS|AIDS]] after the video was found to have violated their respective company's policies about the vaccines. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-technology-health-caribbean-brazil-9abd4832762e9ed405858248547955c3 (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/facebook-takes-down-bolsonaro-video-over-false-vaccine-claim-2021-10-25/ (Reuters)]
